segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, so quick rundown. Cedar Ridge is clean now: 64 seats, standard annual, invoice starts August 1, no redlines.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: They did. Finance was fine with it because the first year is $38,400, paid upfront.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Okay. Anything weird on the week?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: One thing that's making me a little twitchy: Harbor Brands' agreement ends this Friday, July 26, and I don't think anyone from our side has talked to them about carrying on. Like, the paper just stops.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Wait, Harbor with the warehouse forecasting module?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah. Twenty-two users, nine-month term, $24,750. Last actual customer conversation I can see was the June admin training. No renewal thread, no extension language, no, uh, even a casual check-in about whether they keep it on after Friday.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: That's uncomfortable. They're still logging in every day too, right?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Pretty much. Ops had six tickets this month, all normal stuff, but commercially it's just sitting there. If Monday rolls around, we're basically out of contract and nobody will have said anything to Mara about what happens next.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Yeah, not great. Okay. On the other items, did Maple Tooling approve the 15-seat bump?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: They did. Starts September 1, co-termed to their main agreement, $11,250 uplift. Deal desk already blessed the discount staying flat.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Still targeting go-live August 12. They want the training split into two 90-minute sessions because their support team is on shifts, but otherwise it's straightforward.
